children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Wednesday.
WHEAT - Down 1 to 3 cents per bushel
ease on technical selling as crude oil prices weakened. Losses limited by worries about disruptions of Black Sea grain exports and reduced crops in key global production areas.

Wheat production in Canada was projected to fall by 10.9% to 36.1 million metric tons in 2026 compared to 2025, according to a Statistics Canada survey released on Wednesday, based in part on satellite and agroclimatic data.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last down 1-1/2 cents at $7.27 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was down 1-1/4 cents at $7.95 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last 2-1/2 cents higher at $7.51 a bushel.
CORN - Steady to down 2 cents per bushel
futures weaker on lower crude oil prices and a looming U.S. Midwest harvest.
Brazil's 2026/27 corn crop was projected to reach 148 million tons, up 2.8% from the previous season and the largest harvest ever recorded in the country, Brazil's national crop agency Conab said.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last down 1/2 cent at $5.35-1/4 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Up 3 to 9 cents per bushel

higher for a third straight session on good demand for U.S. supplies and as high production costs were expected to curb acreage expansion in Brazil. Expectations for Chinese buying ahead of a meeting between presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump next week underpinned the market.

Brazil's national crop agency Conab said the country's soybean production was expected to rise 0.7% to 181.64 million metric tons in 2026/27. But the planted area was seen expanding by the smallest percentage in two decades.

Canola production in Canada was projected to fall by 0.8% to 22.1 million metric tons in 2026 compared to 2025, according to a Statistics Canada survey released on Wednesday, based in part on satellite and agroclimatic data.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last up 8 cents at $13.26-3/4 per bushel.
